too big yai

noun · Krio (Sierra Leone)
also styled 2BigYai

30 Years. One Kitchen. Brooklyn.

What began as home-cooked lunches delivered to neighbors in Downtown Brooklyn grew into one of the borough's most beloved cultural landmarks. In 1995, founder Pape "Papa" Diagne opened 2BigYai on Fulton Street in Clinton Hill, bringing the bold, soulful flavors of Senegal to a neighborhood that had never tasted anything quite like it.

For over 30 years, the kitchen has stayed true to its roots — slow-braised yassa, hand-rolled fataya, rich mafé — made the way they've always been made, without shortcuts. 2BigYai became more than a restaurant. It became a gathering place, a cultural anchor, a home away from home for Brooklyn's West African community and anyone drawn to its warmth.

Today, 2BigYai stands at 1168 Bedford Avenue in Bed-Stuy, earning recognition from The Infatuation, TripAdvisor, and Foursquare — not because it chased trends, but because it never strayed from what made it great. We are proud to feed Brooklyn, and honored that you're at our table.
